# Change upcoming two-card stack to a face-down deck

## Headline

Replace the visible two-card "Upcoming" incident queue with a face-down incident deck (card back + count): each turn the top card is revealed and resolved at end of turn, deck order is constraint-validated at build/reshuffle time, and a new staff "peek" skill (once per turn, as an action) lets the player look at the top card.

## Problem statement

Main Street shows the next two Incident events face-up in an "Upcoming" panel (`incidentQueue`, `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE = 2`). This removes all suspense about upcoming events and makes the early game trivially predictable. The change replaces visible foresight with a face-down deck — the player knows only how many incidents remain, not what they are — while preserving the fairness constraints and adding a staff skill that gives the player controlled, limited foresight.

## Users / user stories

- **Main Street players** — want suspense and uncertainty about what happens next; a face-down deck adds tension to every end of turn.
  - *As a player, I want upcoming incidents hidden until they resolve, so each turn has suspense and I cannot optimise against known future events.*
- **Main Street players** — want agency despite the hidden deck.
  - *As a player who hired a peeking staff member, I want to peek at the top card of the incident deck once per turn as an action, so I can prepare for (or accept) what is coming.*
- **Game designer / balancer** — the difficulty-tuned draw limits (repeat spacing, good/bad streak) must keep working.
  - *As a designer, I want the constrained-draw balance limits applied to the deck order itself so the face-down deck is no more (un)fair than the visible queue.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Face-down deck replaces the visible queue.** The two face-up "Upcoming" cards are removed: `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE` and the 2-card visible refill loop are gone; the incident source is a face-down deck whose remaining count is the only up-front information (a card back + count in the UI panel). No incident content is visible before its turn.
2. **End-of-turn resolution from the deck top.** Each end of turn reveals and resolves the top card of the incident deck through the existing incident reveal presentation (animation + SFX from `animateIncidentReveal`, CG-0MSRGU8M0009F02C; origin changes from the front queue slot to the deck stack). When the deck is exhausted, event discards reshuffle in (existing `reshuffleIfNeeded`/`forceReshuffleFromDiscards` behavior). Seeded determinism is preserved (same seed ⇒ same deck order and sequence).
3. **Constraint-aware deck ordering (option (a)).** Deck order is fixed at build and at every (re)shuffle so the full pre-arranged draw sequence satisfies `incidentRepeatSpacing` (N) and `incidentMaxStreak` (M) from the difficulty preset / runtime config (`state.incidentBalance`); `recordIncidentDraw` history still tracks the resolved sequence. Constraint violation in any deck built from a valid seed is a unit-testable invariant.
4. **Tutorial, docs, and tests updated.** Tutorial T6 "Upcoming Incidents" is reworded to teach the face-down deck + peek (remove "top happens this turn, below next turn"; update `tutorial-en.ts`, `TutorialFlow.ts`, `TutorialScenario.ts` queue setup, and the tutorial-wording contract test, CG-0MSLXI5MT009CDAP). All related documentation (code comments, help text, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`/`AGENTS.md` where the mechanic is described) is updated. Full project test suite passes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` succeeds.

## Constraints

- **Seeded determinism** must be preserved; RNG-consumption order should not change for unrelated subsystems (deck shuffle is the source of deck order).
- **Balance limits stay runtime-configurable** per difficulty preset (`config.incidentRepeatSpacing` / `incidentMaxStreak`) — do not hard-code new values; legacy saves without those fields keep engine defaults (existing `??` fallback in `createIncidentBalanceState`).
- **View/model separation**: the deck stack should be rendered through the core-engine view components (`PileView` or equivalent) rather than bespoke sprite arrays, per AGENTS.md best practice 2; if the existing panel structure is kept, document why.
- **Audio/visual feedback rule (AGENTS.md rule 8)**: deck-top reveal must animate + play SFX via `SoundManager` (`COMMON_SFX_KEYS`), respecting reduced-motion and mute/volume settings; the peek action should also give lightweight feedback (`popTextOrIcon` acceptable).
- **SLL layout**: the incident panel keeps SLL anchoring (no new hardcoded pixel positioning).
- **Doc-update policy**: developer-facing changes ship with `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (and this file's relevant sections) updated in the same commit; otherwise a doc-update child work item is created and the parent cannot close.
- **Save compatibility**: saved games store `incidentQueue` (`MainStreetState.ts` deserialization path) — the loader must migrate/adapt old saves (e.g. treat saved queue + remaining event deck as the new deck) without crashing mid-game.

## Existing state

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts:685` — `export const INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE = 2`.
- `MainStreetState.ts` — `incidentQueue: EventCard[]` populated at setup via `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE` constraint-aware pre-draws (`findConstrainedIncidentIndex`), saved/restored, `createIncidentBalanceFromQueue` derives balance history from it.
- `MainStreetMarket.ts:505` — `refillIncidentQueue()` tops the queue back up to 2 after each resolve, routing every draw through `findConstrainedIncidentIndex`.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts` — `resolveIncident()` shifts the front queue card, resolves it, then refills.
- `MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `refreshIncidentQueue()` renders up to 2 face-up cards (+ hover tooltips with full effect text) and "Deck: N".
- `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — `animateIncidentReveal()` flies the resolved card from the front queue slot to the log; `MainStreetTurnController.ts` calls it with `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()`.
- Tutorial: `tutorial-en.ts` T6 text ("The event at the top happens at the end of this turn; the ones below happen next turn"), `TutorialFlow.ts` T6 step (confirm gate, `incidentQueue` highlight), `TutorialScenario.ts` builds exactly `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE` queue cards and validates it.
- Staff cards: 7 templates (CSV rows 135–141) providing `handSlotsAdded`, `ongoingCost`, `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount` — no deck-related ability exists.
- Event deck: ~35 Incident-trigger cards + ~21 Investment-trigger cards; investments are pulled into the market at setup; `MAX_TURNS = 20` — an incident-only deck comfortably covers a game.

## Desired change

- Replace the visible FIFO queue with a face-down incident deck (the incident-only subset of the event deck, as today). Remove `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE`; the deck itself is the incident source.
- At setup and at every reshuffle, arrange the deck order so the entire sequence satisfies repeat/streak limits (constraint-aware ordering, seed-driven). `resolveIncident` pops the top card and records its draw history.
- UI: the "Upcoming" panel becomes a face-down stack (card back + remaining count). Reveal animation originates from the deck position.
- New staff "peek" ability: once per turn, as an action, reveal the top card, then return it face-down.
- Update T6 tutorial, save-load migration, and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — remove `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE`; add a constraint-aware deck-ordering helper (e.g. `orderIncidentDeck()`) built on `findConstrainedIncidentIndex`; `StaffCard` peek field (`peekOncePerTurn?: boolean` or similar).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — setup: build/order the incident deck (no pre-drawn queue, or `incidentQueue` repurposed as the deck); state field + save/load migration for old saves.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — `refillIncidentQueue` → deck refill/reshuffle without visible refill loop (or removed; deck exhaustion reshuffles).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `resolveIncident` pops deck top; add `peekIncidentDeck(state)` action + once-per-turn gate.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `refreshIncidentQueue` → face-down stack + count; deck-top center helper for reveal origin.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` / `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — reveal origin from deck stack; peek action/feedback wiring.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` — incident panel geometry for the stack (deck size, count label).
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialScenario.ts` — queue setup → deck setup; validation update.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` + `i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — T6 reword + (optionally) a peek-teaching step.
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — new staff card template with the peek ability.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` (resolveIncident / deck-top / reshuffle), new deck-ordering invariant tests, staff-peek once-per-turn tests, `tutorial-flow.test.ts` / `tutorial-scenario.test.ts` (T6 wording + setup), `activity-log.test.ts` if log messages change.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSL0OP040043KKZ** — Upcoming events: constrained incident draws (repeat spacing + good/bad streak). The constraint machinery is retained and re-applied as deck ordering (option (a)). Completed.
- **CG-0MSL0OU1E005WFJB** — Wire incident-draw balance limits into difficulty presets. Preset/runtime-config interplay must keep working. Completed.
- **CG-0MSRGU8M0009F02C** — Incident reveal presentation (dramatic sting + damage feedback). Reveal animation is reused with a new origin. Completed.
- **CG-0MSTASAX4005FEYL** — Tutorial T6 wording ("top this turn, below next turn"). Superseded by this change; T6 must be reworded. Completed.
- **CG-0MSLXI5MT009CDAP** — 16-step tutorial flow contract (unit). Wording contract enforces T6 content; must be updated in lockstep. Completed.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Truncated producer answer (Q3 "3. yes on …")**: face-down UI (card back + count, top card NOT visible) is an assumption — the change's stated purpose is removing the visible 2-card stack. If the top card should stay visible, AC 1 changes substantially; flagged for producer review.
- **Staff-skill scope assumed in this item** (description lists it under Mechanics). If the producer wants a follow-up, drop AC 4 and create the child.
- **Peek implementation details** (exact card name/cost, peek presentation, whether the peeked card is animated face-up then face-down) are defaults for the implementer; tuning flagged in AC 4.
- **Scope-creep guard**: investment events, market cycles, challenge system, and other staff abilities are untouched. A peek-frequency/strength follow-up (e.g. peek N>1, bury-a-card manipulation) is a possible future item — record as linked work, not scope.
- **Save-load migration risk** (old `incidentQueue` saves): must not corrupt or crash; migration preserves the resolved-sequence fairness where practical.
- **Determinism risk**: constraint-ordered deck building must consume RNG (or not) in a stable, documented order so replays/Monte-Carlo results remain comparable.
- **Perceived fairness**: a purely face-down draw can still produce long bad streaks \*within* the deck cycle unless limits are enforced at build time — AC 3's invariant guards this; verify with the Monte-Carlo harness if order statistics change.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (constrained draw balance):** "The constraint system (incidentRepeatSpacing / incidentMaxStreak) currently picks each incident at refill time based on recent-draw history. A face-down deck fixes the order up-front. Options: (a) enforce constraints at deck-build/shuffle time; (b) enforce only when the deck is reshuffled after exhaustion; (c) drop constraints entirely. Which do you want?"
  - Answer (producer, interactive): **"(a)"** — enforce at deck-build/shuffle time; pre-order the deck so every draw position satisfies the rules; constraints survive; seeded determinism preserved.
  - Evidence: work-item comment `CG-C0MSX3S8QN0092H57` (answer recorded after interactive reply).
- **Q2 (staff skill):** "What should the new deck-related staff skill do — (a) peek at the top N cards (once per turn / once per game / per staff member?), (b) manipulate the deck (bury/discard-and-redraw once per turn), or (c) both? Is it in scope for THIS item or a follow-up?"
  - Answer (producer, interactive): **"(a) — peek at the top of the incident deck, once per turn, as an action."** Scope not explicitly restated; **assumed in-scope** because the item description lists "Add a staff member skill related to the deck" under Mechanics. Flagged for producer review.
  - Evidence: work-item comment `CG-C0MSX3S96Z0060LLQ`; item description.
- **Q3 (deck composition & visibility):** "Should the face-down deck be the incident-only cards from the event deck (as today, ~35 cards), top card revealed+resolved at end of turn, reshuffling discards on exhaustion? And in the UI, completely face-down (card back + count) or top card visible as 'next up'?"
  - Answer (producer, interactive): **"3. yes on …" (truncated)** — affirms the proposed deck composition (incident-only, end-of-turn top-card resolution, reshuffle on exhaustion). UI visibility not explicit; **assumed fully face-down** (card back + count) per the item title/description ("face-down deck", replacing the visible 2-card stack). Flagged for producer review.
  - Evidence: work-item comment `CG-C0MSX3S9MD008V5QZ`.

- **CG-0MSQE2NLX003ADIY** – Main Street: design 50+ new cards of varying types (completed)
- **CG-0MSKSJ9SS0069ZWT** – Main Street tutorial: full text review and step restructure (completed)
